text: Happy to speak for it, Mr. Mayor. I guess a bit of the issue I have with the report as it's been tabled is that it doesn't really differ substantially from the first draft that was presented to us some months ago. It seems to have overridden a lot of the feedback and I note that there was obviously those public meetings and responses were received, but the feedback strongly indicates to me that those affected properties, particularly on the overland flow, the 183 odd properties that are going to have a potential notation on the 10.7 certificates based on this overland flow is a little bit overzealous. As Councillor Williams said, a cookie cutter approach to this issue when you're comparing it to municipalities like the Hawkesbury, Penrith, even Parramatta, which have widespread and substantial flooding issues, you're not comparing apples with apples. I've got folks that live in Windsor who in that same flood event that we saw the graph of earlier in the debate of this motion, had torrents of water pouring through their property. And of course that is seriously flood-prone land. I wouldn't consider Rochor Avenue to be flood-prone land. I also wouldn't consider the possibility of 10% of your property having 15 centimetres of water running across it. Once in 100 years we have those notations put on their title and really that pertains more to the mainstream flooding properties that essentially we are putting a blanket overland flow notation on 10.7 certificates for a lot of people that will not be substantially affected by flooding, haven't been substantially affected by flooding. And not only is that going to lower their house prices and up their insurance premiums, what it's going to do is subject them potentially to flood-related development controls in the future. And they're not going to take any solace in the fact that that is being done to them as a result of the potential for 10% of their property to be flooded once in 100 years. Now, out of that, there will be genuine overland flow issues and I think that there will be some residents that want to take advantage of the funding that may come with their properties being registered as flood prone. But for the vast majority and the feedback that I've had from residents and the feedback that I think we can get out of the community consultation is the majority don't feel that their properties are going to be affected in the way that the report has indicated. And I don't think that that cookie cutter approach is going to serve as well in Hunters Hill as it does in those areas like Parramatta and Hawkesbury and Penrith, which have widespread problems with greenfield sites, for example, exporting and importing fill. So I think we need to step back and look at what flood mitigation we can do in the next stages of this process, but also how serious we want to be about putting notifications on people's 10.7 certificates in the knowledge that it really does affect the prices of their property and it really will affect not only their capacity to improve their properties, but also their insurance premiums. And I don't think slapping it on 183 odd titles for overland flood mitigation and 183 odd titles for overland flow is going to be something welcomed in the community. So I can only recommend that this motion be brought forward and particularly given that it's asking in point seven to seek relevant advice from the state government agency as to whether or not we can have a broad compliance approach to the flood study. And I think that other local government areas have had an approach that is unique to their topography and their local government area. And I think that's something that we need to explore here because blanketing 180 odd homes with this notation on their 10.7 certificates is not going to be something that's welcomed, particularly for residents that are not going to be substantially affected by flooding and some of which who have lived in the area for a very long time and have observed that there is no real flood affected in nature to their properties. So I think that this is a sensible way to have a merit-based flood study as we progress out of the study stages and into the implementation stages of our flood planning. But I think-
